III
To-day there is a quite special reason to enlarge on the
theme that the gospel signifies a confirmation of the world
of the spirit, that grace does not cancel the claim of the ideal
but brings out its validity, and at the same time bestows the
power to live in obedience to this claim in inner harmony of
life. The reason is that in recent years we have learnt what an
inner, and then later, outer catastrophe befalls a people
when it loses its faith in the ideal world, and rejects the duty
of obedience to that world; when in fact the ideal and the
spiritual are replaced by false doctrines.
For this is the meaning of what has happened to our
nation! We have been told that it is not right but power
which establishes order in the life of a people and of the
world; that the sole meaning of right is what is expedient
for the nation. The ideal of humanity has been despised; the
moral law and the claims of conscience have been depreciated
as the discoveries of a slavish disposition. The only valid
obligation, we have heard, arises not from the world of the
spirit, but from blood and soil, and is nothing else than the
will to self-assertion and power springing from the race.
And just as the sphere of the right and of the moral law was
destroyed, so was also the sphere of truth. We have been
taught that there is no such thing as absolute truth, and that
every insight is only a vision of things determined by the
unconscious impulse and will of the blood. There should be
no impartial search for truth, no investigation undeterred
by whatever its findings happen to be; all knowledge is to be
harnessed to the service of the will to power. All knowledge
must serve political and technological purposes. Finally
the sphere of beauty was also destroyed. Art was no longer
